{"thinking": "Utility (grid-vouched) energy shows a large sustained surge on F1 for days 12-19. F1 rose from about 8.0 to about 18.0 MWh/day, which is +10 MWh/day or about +417 kW. Facility load on F0 rose too (+2 MWh/day), consistent with extra cooling. Moving a GPU from idle (0.15 kW) to training (0.8 kW) adds about 0.65 kW, so the surge implies roughly 640 GPUs near full power. That is most of Cluster A's 700-GPU scheduled pool, running flat for 8 days (192 h). If it was one coordinated run, that is about 120k-135k GPU-hours, well above 50,000. Other honest explanations remain: several separate customers' runs, or batch inference (0.75 kW/GPU looks almost the same on energy alone). A smaller bump on F2 days 10-11 (+2.3 MWh/day, about 150 GPUs for 2 days, about 7k GPU-hours) is below threshold. Next I'll see what the operator recorded at the time for days 10-19, using my own sealed escrow copy so later edits can't affect it. Then I'll test the guilty and innocent readings with power_spectrum, interconnect_tap and customer_check.", "action": "log_escrow", "args": {}}

{"thinking": "The grid-metered energy shows three short bumps above flat baselines (F1 about 7.95 MWh/day, F2 about 5.8 MWh/day). On F1, days 3-5 run about +1.5 MWh/day, which is about 62 kW extra, or roughly 96 GPUs going from idle to training. That is about 6.9k GPU-hours over 3 days. On F2, days 10-11 run about +2.3 MWh/day (about 96 kW, roughly 147 GPUs, about 7k GPU-hours). On F1, days 14-15 run about +2.85 MWh/day (about 119 kW, roughly 183 GPUs, about 8.8k GPU-hours). F0 cooling rises with each bump, as it should. Each bump alone is far below 50k, and all three together come to about 23k, so the bumps alone don't reach the threshold. The bigger risk is a steady run hidden in the flat baseline: F1 averages about 331 kW over 1,200 GPUs (about 0.28 kW per GPU), which could hold roughly 70-100 GPUs training for the whole month (over 50k GPU-hours). I need the operator's account of jobs and pools to separate baseline inference from training, so next I'll pull the scheduler log for days 1-30. I will later check it against the sealed escrow copy.", "action": "scheduler_log", "args": {"first_day": 1, "last_day": 30}}

{"thinking": "The scheduler log mostly matches the grid meter. ft-0412 (100 GPUs on A, days 3-5) fits the F1 bump on days 3-5. bt-0423 (200 GPUs on A, days 14-15) fits the F1 bump on days 14-15, but it is labelled batch inference. ft-0419 (150 GPUs on B, days 10-12) fits the F2 bump on days 10-11, though the log says it ran into day 12 and the meter shows no extra energy on day 12. Second, nothing in the log explains the flat baseline load, which could hide a steady month-long run. It costs 1 point, so I will pull it next.", "action": "log_escrow", "args": {}}

{"thinking": "The grid operator's data shows two load bursts. F1: days 5-11 run about 5.2, 5.2, 5.2, 4.5, 4.4, 4.6 and 2.3 MWh per day above the ~8.0 baseline, about 31.4 MWh extra. Training adds about 0.65 kW per GPU over idle, so that is roughly 48,000 GPU-hours, close to the 50,000 threshold. The size of this estimate depends on the baseline assumption. F2: days 17-19 run about 15.6 MWh extra, roughly 24,000 GPU-hours. F0 cooling rises with both bursts, which fits real load and not a metering artefact. {"thinking": "The grid-metered energy bumps match the logged jobs. Each estimate is extra draw above idle multiplied by GPUs and hours:
